title: SakugaFlow: A Stagewise Illustration Framework Emulating the Human Drawing Process and Providing Interactive Tutoring for Novice Drawing Skills
venue: GenAICHI: CHI 2025 Workshop on Generative AI and HCI
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the gap between generative image tools that produce finished illustrations and the learning needs of novice artists who need to understand how drawings are constructed step by step. The authors argue that current text-to-image and editing systems are effective for output generation but do not reveal the intermediate stages that could help beginners learn foundational illustration skills such as anatomy, perspective, composition, and color harmony.

To address this, the paper presents SakugaFlow, a stagewise illustration framework that emulates a human drawing workflow. The system breaks illustration into four stages—rough sketch, line art, coloring, and final finishing—using diffusion-based generation at each stage. An LLM-based tutoring agent provides real-time advice, explanations, and localized revision guidance as users progress through the stages. Users can also branch versions, inpaint regions, and compare alternatives within the same project.

The intended population is novice illustrators or beginners learning drawing skills, likely adults rather than K-12 learners, and the context is interactive creative software rather than a classroom intervention. The paper is primarily a design and systems proposal presented at a HCI workshop, not an evaluation study with human participants. Its main conclusion is that staged generation plus conversational tutoring could turn generative AI from a black-box image generator into a scaffolded learning partner for skill development, although the authors note that controlled user studies are needed in future work to test learning outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a workshop-style system proposal/prototype paper rather than an empirical study. It presents the design of SakugaFlow and discusses future evaluation plans, but reports no controlled user study, quantitative learning outcomes, or comparative evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: No measurable educational impact is reported. The paper offers a conceptual intervention for novice drawing support, but provides no effect sizes or evidence of learning gains, so impact on K-12 outcomes is currently unknown.

interventions.use_case: An LLM-powered tutor embedded in a staged illustration workflow provides real-time feedback, explanations, and guidance on anatomy, perspective, composition, color theory, and localized revisions for novice drawing practice.

A stagewise illustration interface adapts the drawing process through rough sketch, line art, coloring, and finishing stages, allowing branching, backtracking, and inpainting based on user progress and edits.

An interactive drawing support system delivers step-by-step instructional scaffolding through staged visual outputs and prompts, but the paper does not evaluate a formal tutoring algorithm or learning outcomes.
